A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ResCLIP research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material. All 17 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResCLIP segmentation results, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original segmentation experiments and adds inference-speed and computational-cost measurements in Appendix D, Table A3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same RCS attention aggregation and residual fusion, SFR semantic-mask refinement, and final inference procedure. Equations (1)–(13) are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight segmentation benchmark settings across PASCAL VOC, PASCAL Context, COCO Object/Stuff, Cityscapes, and ADE20K. The added efficiency evaluation uses the existing VOC20 task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. The new efficiency table reuses CLIP, NACLIP, and the already evaluated RCS-only, SFR-only, and combined ResCLIP variants.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds an efficiency evaluation measuring images per second and FLOPs on VOC20 with CLIP-ViT-B/16, a single RTX 3090, batch size 1, 336×336 input, and fp16. Existing segmentation evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table A3 adds a componentwise analysis of computational overhead, separating RCS-only, SFR-only, and combined costs. Existing accuracy ablations, layer-fusion and hyperparameter analyses, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new efficiency table also reports point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports speed and FLOPs in Table A3, including NACLIP at 32.3 images/s and 41.8G FLOPs versus combined ResCLIP at 28.9 images/s and 44.8G FLOPs. Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and A1–A2, and the qualitative findings, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Section 3 are retained. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about intermediate-layer localization, training-free RCS/SFR, plug-and-play integration, and improved segmentation performance.

C2.justification: New Appendix D attributes limited overhead to reusing intermediate attentions and lightweight final-layer refinement, describes the speed impact as negligible, and notes that SFR implementation could be optimized. v1 contains no corresponding cost interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the GPU, batch size, input resolution, and numerical precision for the new efficiency measurements. Existing implementation information, preprocessing, prompts, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research and positioning are unchanged. The reduction from 63 to 62 references consolidates duplicate ViT citations; other changes update author lists and publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered wording and bibliographic corrections, adds acknowledgments, and inserts Appendix D on efficiency. The previous visualization section becomes Appendix E; the main narrative and organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A3 and reflows the surrounding appendix text. Existing figures and tables retain their content and basic displays, with limited spacing, caption, and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: Appendix D and Table A3 fill a modest reporting gap by quantifying component costs and documenting measurement conditions, making practical tradeoffs easier to assess. Earlier accuracy evidence is preserved. The benefit is tempered by optimistic wording: the claimed negligible speed impact includes approximately 10.5% lower throughput than NACLIP, from 32.3 to 28.9 images/s.
